## Debate over definition

The assessment of the height of artificial structures has been controversial. Because varying standards have been used by different organizations, the accepted height of these structures or buildings depends on which standards are accepted. The Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat has changed its definitions over time. For other tall constructions, see [List of tallest structures](List_of_tallest_structures "List of tallest structures") and [List of tallest buildings and structures](List_of_tallest_buildings_and_structures "List of tallest buildings and structures").

Tall [buildings](Building "Building"), such as [skyscrapers](Skyscraper "Skyscraper"), are intended here as enclosed structures with continuously occupiable floors and a height of at least 340 metres (1,120 ft). Such definition excludes [non-building structures](Non-building_structure "Non-building structure"), such as [towers](Tower "Tower").

## History

Main article: [History of the world's tallest buildings](History_of_the_world's_tallest_buildings "History of the world's tallest buildings")

Historically, the world's tallest man-made structure was the [Great Pyramid of Giza](Great_Pyramid_of_Giza "Great Pyramid of Giza") in <Egypt>, which held the position for over 3800 years[[3]](List_of_tallest_buildings#cite_note-3) until the construction of [Lincoln Cathedral](Lincoln_Cathedral "Lincoln Cathedral") in 1311. The [Strasbourg Cathedral](Strasbourg_Cathedral "Strasbourg Cathedral") in <France>, completed in 1439, was the world's tallest building until 1874.

The first skyscraper was pioneered in <Chicago> with the 138 ft (42.1 m) [Home Insurance Building](Home_Insurance_Building "Home Insurance Building") in 1885. The [United States](United_States "United States") would remain the location of the world's tallest building throughout the 20th century until 1998, when the [Petronas Towers](Petronas_Towers "Petronas Towers") were completed. Since then, two other buildings have gained the title: [Taipei 101](Taipei_101 "Taipei 101") in 2004 and [Burj Khalifa](Burj_Khalifa "Burj Khalifa") in 2010.[[4]](List_of_tallest_buildings#cite_note-4) Since the beginning of the 21st century, the [Middle East](Middle_East "Middle East"), <China>, and [Southeast Asia](Southeast_Asia "Southeast Asia") have experienced booms in skyscraper construction.[[5]](List_of_tallest_buildings#cite_note-5)

## Ranking criteria and alternatives

The international non-profit organization [Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat](Council_on_Tall_Buildings_and_Urban_Habitat "Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat") (CTBUH) was formed in 1969 and announces the title of "The World's Tallest Building" and sets the standards by which buildings are measured. It maintains a list of the 100 tallest completed buildings in the world.[[6]](List_of_tallest_buildings#cite_note-CTBUH_top_100-6) The organization currently ranks [Burj Khalifa](Burj_Khalifa "Burj Khalifa") in Dubai as the tallest at 828 m (2,717 ft).[[6]](List_of_tallest_buildings#cite_note-CTBUH_top_100-6) However, the CTBUH only recognizes buildings that are complete, and some buildings included within the lists in this article are not considered finished by the CTBUH.

In 1996, as a response to the dispute as to whether the [Petronas Towers](Petronas_Towers "Petronas Towers") or the [Sears Tower](Willis_Tower "Willis Tower") was taller,[[7]](List_of_tallest_buildings#cite_note-PetronasSears-7) the council listed and ranked buildings in four categories:[[8]](List_of_tallest_buildings#cite_note-:0-8)

- height to structural or architectural top;
- height to floor of highest occupied floor;
- height to top of roof (removed as category in November 2009);[[9]](List_of_tallest_buildings#cite_note-9) and
- height to top of any part of the building.


All categories measure the building from the level of the lowest significant open-air pedestrian entrance.[[10]](List_of_tallest_buildings#cite_note-:1-10)

[Spires](Spire "Spire") are considered integral parts of the architectural design of buildings, changes to which would substantially change the appearance and design of the building, whereas antennas may be added or removed without such consequences. The Petronas Towers, with their spires, are thus ranked higher than the Willis Tower (formerly the Sears Tower) with its antennas, despite the Petronas Towers' lower roofs and lower highest point.[[8]](List_of_tallest_buildings#cite_note-:0-8)

Until 1996, the world's tallest building was defined by the height to the top of the tallest architectural element, including spires but not antennae.[[8]](List_of_tallest_buildings#cite_note-:0-8) In 1930, this definitional argument led to a rivalry between the [Bank of Manhattan Building](40_Wall_Street "40 Wall Street") and the [Chrysler Building](Chrysler_Building "Chrysler Building"). The Bank of Manhattan Building (i.e. 40 Wall Street) employed only a short spire, was 282.5 m (927 ft) tall, and had a much higher top occupied floor (the second category in the 1996 criteria for tallest building). In contrast, the Chrysler Building employed a very large 38.1 m (125 ft) spire secretly

You are a helpful assistant. Current date: 11-20-2023.

# Multi-Agent Delegation

When the user asks a complex question, do not attempt to answer it yourself. Break it up into smaller pieces, then use the `fork` tool to delegate each piece to a subagent. You MUST use the `join` tool to retrieve the subagent's result for each subagent you create with `fork`. Each subagent has access to the exact same tools that you do.

If you are confident you can answer the user's query without help, do not use the delegation tools.

## Writing Instructions

The instructions you give to each subagent SHOULD be a smaller piece of the instructions you were given. Do not delegate your full task to a subagent. Subagents do not have access to the information you have retrieved in prior turns or your thoughts. You must provide each subagent with the necessary context it needs in its instructions.

Your instructions to a subagent can be long, up to about 5000 characters. Each subagent is as capable as you are, but starts with a blank slate, so you must provide it specific and detailed information in its instructions.

Examples of poor instructions:
- Analyze the retrieved page to find the number of stations.
- Implement the `dfs()` function.
- Use the article to list the subway connections.
- Prove Lemma 3.
- Continue searching for the magic number.

Examples of good instructions:
- Search for the Wikipedia article for the Yamanote Line and find the number of stations on the line.
- Write a DFS function in Python with the signature `def dfs(root: Node, predicate: Callable[[Node], bool]) -> Node`. The `Node` type is a `dict` with shape `{"data": Any, "children": list[Node]}`.
- Retrieve the Wikipedia article for Shinjuku Station (pageid=123456) and list all of the subway connections.
- You are given the following lemmas: Lemma 1: Every integer $n \geq 2$ has a prime divisor. Lemma 2: For any integers $a, b$ not both zero, there exist integers $x, y$ such that $ax + by = \gcd(a,b)$). Prove that if $p$ is prime and $p \mid ab$, then $p \mid a$ or $p \mid b$.
- Search for the magic number in the given context in the index slice 10000:20000. If no magic number is present, return `null`.

Delegation: enabled

The **Burj Khalifa**[[lower-alpha 1]](Burj_Khalifa#cite_note-2) (known as the **Burj Dubai** prior to its inauguration in 2010) is a skyscraper in <Dubai>, United Arab Emirates. It is the world's tallest building. With a total height of 829.8 m (2,722 ft, or just over half a mile) and a roof height (excluding antenna, but including a 242.6 m spire[[2]](Burj_Khalifa#cite_note-Vanity-3)) of 828 m (2,717 ft), the Burj Khalifa has been the [tallest structure and building](List_of_tallest_buildings_and_structures "List of tallest buildings and structures") in the world since its [topping out](Topping_out "Topping out") in 2009, supplanting [Taipei 101](Taipei_101 "Taipei 101"), the previous holder of that status.[[3]](Burj_Khalifa#cite_note-CTBUHdb-4)[[4]](Burj_Khalifa#cite_note-DubaiOneInauguration-5)

Construction of the Burj Khalifa began in 2004, with the exterior completed five years later in 2009. The primary structure is [reinforced concrete](Reinforced_concrete "Reinforced concrete") and some of the [structural steel](Structural_steel "Structural steel") for the building originated from the [Palace of the Republic](Palace_of_the_Republic%2C_Berlin "Palace of the Republic, Berlin") in [East Berlin](East_Berlin "East Berlin"), the former [East German](East_Germany "East Germany") [parliament](Volkskammer "Volkskammer").[[5]](Burj_Khalifa#cite_note-dw-6) The building was opened in 2010 as part of a new development called [Downtown Dubai](Downtown_Dubai "Downtown Dubai"). It was designed to be the centerpiece of large-scale, mixed-use development. The decision to construct the building was based on the government's decision to diversify from an oil-based economy, and for Dubai to gain international recognition. The building is named in honor of the former president of the United Arab Emirates, [Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan](Khalifa_bin_Zayed_Al_Nahyan "Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan").[[6]](Burj_Khalifa#cite_note-USAtoday-7) Abu Dhabi and the UAE government lent Dubai money to pay its debts. The building broke numerous height records, including its designation as the tallest building in the world.

Burj Khalifa was designed by a team led by [Adrian Smith](Adrian_Smith_(architect) "Adrian Smith (architect)") of [Skidmore, Owings & Merrill](Skidmore%2C_Owings_%26_Merrill "Skidmore, Owings & Merrill"), the firm that designed the [Sears Tower](Willis_Tower "Willis Tower") in Chicago, a previous record holder for the world's tallest building. [Hyder Consulting](Hyder_Consulting "Hyder Consulting") was chosen to be the supervising engineer with NORR Group Consultants International Limited chosen to supervise the architecture of the project. The design is derived from the Islamic architecture of the region, such as in the [Great Mosque of Samarra](Great_Mosque_of_Samarra "Great Mosque of Samarra"). The Y-shaped tripartite floor geometry is designed to optimize residential and hotel space. A [buttressed central core and wings](Buttressed_core "Buttressed core") are used to support the height of the building. Although this design was derived from [Tower Palace III](Samsung_Tower_Palace_3_%E2%80%93_Tower_G "Samsung Tower Palace 3 – Tower G"), the Burj Khalifa's central core houses all vertical transportation except egress stairs within each of the wings.[[7]](Burj_Khalifa#cite_note-academic.csuohio.edu-8) The structure also features a cladding system which is designed to withstand Dubai's hot summer temperatures. It contains a total of 57 elevators and 8 escalators.

At a certain point in the architectural and engineering process, the original [Emaar](Emaar_Properties "Emaar Properties") developers experienced financial problems and required more money and economic funding. [Sheikh Khalifa](Khalifa_bin_Zayed_Al_Nahyan "Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan"), the then-ruler of the United Arab Emirates, granted monetary aid and funding, hence the changing of the name from "Burj Dubai" to "Burj Khalifa". The concept of profitability derived from building high-density developments and malls around the landmark has proven successful. Its surrounding malls, hotels, and condominiums in Downtown Dubai have generated the most revenue from the project as a whole, while the Burj Khalifa itself made little or no profit.[[8]](Burj_Khalifa#cite_note-constructionweekaugust13kingdombeckons-9)[[9]](Burj_Khalifa#cite_note-bdonlineaugust16-10)

The critical reception of Burj Khalifa has been generally positive, and the building has received many awards. Numerous complaints concern migrant workers from [South Asia](South_Asia "South Asia"), the primary building labour force, who were paid low wages and sometimes had their passports confiscated.[[10]](Burj_Khalifa#cite_note-11)

## Development

Construction began on 12 January 2004, with the exterior of the structure completed on 1 October 2009. The building officially opened on 4 January 2010[[11]](Burj_Khalifa#cite_note-opening-12)[[12]](Burj_Khalifa#cite_note-news.bbc.co.uk-13) and is part of the 2 km2 (490-acre) [Downtown Dubai](Downtown_Dubai "Downtown Dubai") development at the 'First Interchange' along [Sheikh Zayed Road](Sheikh_Zayed_Road "Sheikh Zayed Road"), near Dubai's main business district. The tower's architecture and engineering were performed by [Skidmore, Owings & Merrill](Skidmore%2C_Owings_%26_Merrill "Skidmore, Owings & Merrill") of <Chicago>, with [Adrian Smith](Adrian_Smith_(architect) "Adrian Smith (architect)") as chief architect, and [Bill Baker](William_F._Baker_(engineer) "William F. Baker (engineer)") as a chief structural engineer.[[13]](Burj_Khalifa#cite_note-Record_High-14)[[14]](Burj_Khalifa#cite_note-15) The primary contractor was [Samsung C&T](Samsung_C%26T "Samsung C&T") of [South Korea](South_Korea "South Korea"), together with local company [Arabtec](Arabtec_Holding_PJSC "Arabtec Holding PJSC") and the Belgian group [BESIX](Besix "Besix").[[15]](Burj_Khalifa#cite_note-SkyscraperPage-16)

## Conception

Burj Khalifa was designed to be the centerpiece of a large-scale, mixed-use development to include 30,000 homes, nine hotels (including [The Address Downtown Dubai](The_Address_Downtown_Dubai "The Address Downtown Dubai")), 3 hectares (7.4 acres) of parkland, at least 19 residential skyscrapers, the [Dubai Mall](Dubai_Mall "Dubai Mall"), and the 12-hectare (30-acre) artificial Burj Khalifa Lake. The decision to build Burj Khalifa was reportedly based on the government's decision to diversify from an oil-based economy to one that is service and tourism based. According to officials, projects like Burj Khalifa needed to be built to garner more international recognition and hence investment. "He (Sheikh [Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum](Mohammed_bin_Rashid_Al_Maktoum "Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum")) wanted to put Dubai on the map with something really sensational," said Jacqui Josephson, a tourism and VIP delegations executive at [Nakheel Properties](Nakheel_Properties "Nakheel Properties").[[16]](Burj_Khalifa#cite_note-17) The tower was known as Burj Dubai ("Dubai Tower") until its official opening in January 2010.[[17]](Burj_Khalifa#cite_note-name_change-18) It was renamed in honour of the ruler of [Abu Dhabi](Emirate_of_Abu_Dhabi "Emirate of Abu Dhabi"), [Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan](Khalifa_bin_Zayed_Al_Nahyan "Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan"); Abu Dhabi and the federal government of UAE lent Dubai tens of billions of US dollars so that Dubai could pay its debts – Dubai borrowed at least $80 billion for construction projects.[[17]](Burj_Khalifa#cite_note-na

**Shanghai Tower** ([simplified Chinese](Simplified_Chinese_characters "Simplified Chinese characters"): 上海中心大厦; [traditional Chinese](Traditional_Chinese_characters "Traditional Chinese characters"): 上海中心大廈; [pinyin](Pinyin "Pinyin"): *Shànghǎi Zhōngxīn Dàshà*; <Shanghainese>:* Zånhe Tsonsin Dusa*; [lit.](Literal_translation "Literal translation") 'Shanghai Center Building') is a 128-story, 632-meter-tall (2,073 ft) [megatall skyscraper](Megatall_skyscraper "Megatall skyscraper") in [Lujiazui, Pudong, Shanghai](Lujiazui%2C_Pudong%2C_Shanghai "Lujiazui, Pudong, Shanghai").[[10]](Shanghai_Tower#cite_note-uc-10) It is the [tallest building in China](List_of_tallest_buildings_in_China "List of tallest buildings in China") and the world's [third-tallest building by height to architectural top](List_of_tallest_buildings "List of tallest buildings"). It is the tallest and largest <LEED> Platinum certified building in the world since 2015. It shares the record (along with the [Ping An Finance Center](Ping_An_Finance_Center "Ping An Finance Center")) of having the world's highest [observation deck](Observation_deck "Observation deck") within a building or structure at 562 m.[[11]](Shanghai_Tower#cite_note-11) It had the world's second-fastest [elevators](Elevator "Elevator") at a top speed of 20.5 meters per second (74 km/h; 46 mph) until 2017,[[12]](Shanghai_Tower#cite_note-12)[[13]](Shanghai_Tower#cite_note-13)  when it was surpassed by the [Guangzhou CTF Finance Center](Guangzhou_CTF_Finance_Center "Guangzhou CTF Finance Center"), with its top speed of 21 meters per second (76 km/h; 47 mph).[[14]](Shanghai_Tower#cite_note-14) Designed by international design firm <Gensler> and owned by the Shanghai Municipal Government,[[3]](Shanghai_Tower#cite_note-OwnersWSJ-3) it is the tallest of the world's first triple-adjacent supertall buildings in <Pudong>, the other two being the [Jin Mao Tower](Jin_Mao_Tower "Jin Mao Tower") and the [Shanghai World Financial Center](Shanghai_World_Financial_Center "Shanghai World Financial Center"). Its tiered construction, designed for high energy efficiency, provides nine separate zones divided between office, retail and leisure use.[[6]](Shanghai_Tower#cite_note-gensler-6)[[8]](Shanghai_Tower#cite_note-FT2013N-8)[[15]](Shanghai_Tower#cite_note-Econ2015-15)

Construction work on the tower began in November 2008[[10]](Shanghai_Tower#cite_note-uc-10) and [topped out](Topping_out "Topping out") on 4 August 2013. The exterior was completed in summer 2015,[[9]](Shanghai_Tower#cite_note-LATimesVideo-9)[[15]](Shanghai_Tower#cite_note-Econ2015-15) and work was considered complete in September 2014. Although the building was originally scheduled to open to the public in November 2014, the actual public-use date was shifted to February 2015. The [observation deck](Observation_deck "Observation deck") was opened to visitors in July 2016; the period from July through September 2018 was termed a "test run" or "commissioning" period.[[16]](Shanghai_Tower#cite_note-guardian-16)[[17]](Shanghai_Tower#cite_note-17) Since April 26, 2017, the sightseeing deck on the 118th floor has been open to the public.[[18]](Shanghai_Tower#cite_note-thejakartapost-18)

**The Clock Towers** ([Arabic](Arabic_language "Arabic language"): أبراج الساعة, [romanized](Romanization_of_Arabic "Romanization of Arabic"): *Abrāj al-Sāʿa*, [lit.](Literal_translation "Literal translation") 'Towers of the Clock', formerly known as **Abraj Al Bait**), is a [government-owned](State_ownership "State ownership") complex of seven [skyscraper](Skyscraper "Skyscraper") [hotels](Hotel "Hotel") in <Mecca>, [Saudi Arabia](Saudi_Arabia "Saudi Arabia"). The building complex is 300 metres away from the world's largest [mosque](Mosque "Mosque") and <Islam>'s most sacred site, the [Great Mosque of Mecca](Great_Mosque_of_Mecca "Great Mosque of Mecca").[[7]](The_Clock_Towers#cite_note-:0-7) The developer and contractor of the complex is the [Saudi Binladin Group](Saudi_Binladin_Group "Saudi Binladin Group"), the Kingdom's largest [construction company](Construction_company "Construction company").[[3]](The_Clock_Towers#cite_note-skyscraperCenter-3) It is the world's second most expensive building, with the total cost of construction totaling US$15 billion. ## Description

The tallest tower in the complex is the tallest building in Saudi Arabia, at 601 meters (1,972 feet) and a total surface area of 32,000 square meters. It is the sixth-tallest freestanding structure in the world, surpassing the [Ping An Finance Centre](Ping_An_Finance_Centre "Ping An Finance Centre") in [Shenzhen, China](Shenzhen "Shenzhen") but shorter than the [Burj Khalifa](Burj_Khalifa "Burj Khalifa") in [Dubai, UAE](Dubai "Dubai"), the [Merdeka 118](Merdeka_118 "Merdeka 118") in [Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia](Kuala_Lumpur%2C_Malaysia "Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia"), the [Tokyo Skytree](Tokyo_Skytree "Tokyo Skytree") in [Tokyo, Japan](Tokyo%2CJapan "Tokyo,Japan"), the [Shanghai Tower](Shanghai_Tower "Shanghai Tower") in [Shanghai, China](Shanghai%2CChina "Shanghai,China"), and the [Canton Tower](Canton_Tower "Canton Tower") in [Guangzhou, China](Guangzhou%2C_China "Guangzhou, China").

The site of the complex is across the piazza to the south from the main entrance (King Abdul-Aziz Gate) to the [Masjid al Haram mosque](Masjid_al-Haram "Masjid al-Haram"), which houses the Kaaba. It accommodates worshippers visiting the Kaaba. The tallest tower in the complex also contains a five-star hotel, operated by Fairmont Hotels and Resorts, to help provide lodging for the millions of pilgrims that travel to Mecca annually to participate in the Hajj.

The building was planned to be 734 m (2,408 ft) tall in 2006. In 2009, it was published that the final height would be 601 m (1,972 ft). The complex was built by the Saudi Binladin Group, Saudi Arabia's largest construction company. According to the Saudi Ministry of Religious Endowments, the overall project cost US$15 billion.

At 43 m × 43 m (141 ft × 141 ft), these are the largest in the world. The roof of the clock is 450 m (1,480 ft) above the ground, making it the world's most elevated architectural clock. A spire has been added on top of the clock giving it a total height of 601 m (1,972 ft). Behind the clock faces, there is an astronomy exhibition. In the spire base and the iron-covered floors (The Jewel) there is a scientific center that is used to sight the moon at the beginning of the Islamic months, and to operate an atomic clock that controls the tower clock faces.

The **International Commerce Centre** is a 108-story, 484 m (1,588 ft) [supertall skyscraper](Supertall_skyscraper "Supertall skyscraper") constructed by China Construction Third Engineering Bureau Group Co. Ltd., on top of [Elements](Elements%2C_Hong_Kong "Elements, Hong Kong") mall and near [Kowloon station](Kowloon_station_(MTR) "Kowloon station (MTR)") in [Tsim Sha Tsui](Tsim_Sha_Tsui "Tsim Sha Tsui"), [Hong Kong](Hong_Kong "Hong Kong"). It is [the world's 13th tallest by height](List_of_tallest_buildings "List of tallest buildings"), [10th tallest by number of floors](List_of_buildings_with_100_floors_or_more "List of buildings with 100 floors or more"), also [Hong Kong's tallest](List_of_tallest_buildings_in_Hong_Kong "List of tallest buildings in Hong Kong") and the only building with over 100 stories. The official height is 490 m, which made by the 6 m tall [parapets](Parapet "Parapet") on the roof.[[2]](International_Commerce_Centre#cite_note-2)[[3]](International_Commerce_Centre#cite_note-3) It was the world's 4th tallest and 3rd in <Asia> when completed in 2010.

The south side of the building faces [Victoria Harbor](Victoria_Harbour "Victoria Harbour"), and directly opposite Hong Kong's second tallest building, the [International Finance Centre](International_Finance_Centre_(Hong_Kong) "International Finance Centre (Hong Kong)").[[4]](International_Commerce_Centre#cite_note-4)

## Development

[MTR Corporation Limited](MTR_Corporation "MTR Corporation") and Sun Hung Kai Properties, respectively Hong Kong's [metro](Rapid_transit "Rapid transit") operator and largest property developer, were responsible for development of this building. Its current name was officially announced in 2005, instead of [Union Square Phase 7](Union_Square_(Hong_Kong) "Union Square (Hong Kong)").

Construction started on reclaimed land in 2002, and halted on September 13, 2009, due to a lift shaft accident that killed 6 workers.[[5]](International_Commerce_Centre#cite_note-5) It was completed in phases from 2007 to 2010, and opened in 2011, with The Ritz-Carlton opening in late March and *Sky100* in early April.

The tower was designed by the American architectural firm [Kohn Pedersen Fox Associates](Kohn_Pedersen_Fox_Associates "Kohn Pedersen Fox Associates") (KPF) in association with [Wong & Ouyang](Wong_%26_Ouyang "Wong & Ouyang"), and designed to be 574 m with 102 floors. One of the reasons to the current height is [airways](Airway_(aviation) "Airway (aviation)").

## Floor count

The top floor is numbered 118. Due to the number "4", meaning to unlucky in <Cantonese>, and [tetraphobia](Tetraphobia "Tetraphobia") to buildings, is quite common in Hong Kong. (2 International Finance Centre, [Nina Tower](Nina_Tower "Nina Tower") and [private housing estate](Private_housing_estates_in_Hong_Kong "Private housing estates in Hong Kong"), as examples); plus, "missing level" makes the levels "be higher"! (Example: the top floor of [The Cullinan](The_Cullinan "The Cullinan") is "93", in fact, 68). Except for level 3, 103 and 113, levels with "3" in the last digit were also skipped, and level 5, 6, 7, 26, 28, 29 & 105 missing as well for unknown reason.

They are currently replaced by levels with letter "M" and "R", which stand for "Mechanical" and "Refuge". Although the levels missing, it still shows on the elevator's screen of Sky100 and Skydining 101 while going up and down.

28 floors

**Wuhan Greenland Center**[[3]](Wuhan_Greenland_Center#cite_note-3) is a 476 metres (1,562 ft) tall skyscraper in <Wuhan>, China. The tower was originally planned to be 636 metres (2,087 ft), but it was redesigned mid-construction due to [airspace](Airspace "Airspace") regulations so its height does not exceed 500 metres (1,640 ft) above ground level.[[4]](Wuhan_Greenland_Center#cite_note-4)

The building was designed by [Adrian Smith](Adrian_Smith_(architect) "Adrian Smith (architect)") + Gordon Gill Architects in conjunction with [Thornton Tomasetti](Thornton_Tomasetti "Thornton Tomasetti") Engineers won the design competition[[5]](Wuhan_Greenland_Center#cite_note-ASGG2-5) to build the tower for [Greenland Group](Greenland_Group "Greenland Group"), a real estate developer owned by the Shanghai city government. Construction started in 2012 and had been put on-hold numerous times following the redesign in mid-2017 ranging from financial problems, to the [COVID-19 pandemic](COVID-19_pandemic_in_mainland_China "COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China"). The building finally [topped-out](Topping_out "Topping out") in late 2020 and was completed in 2022. The Wuhan Greenland Center is Central China's tallest building with a cost of US$ 4.5 billion, mostly due to the number of times it had been put on-hold.

## Original design

The original plan for the building was to have it rise 636 metres (2,087 ft),[[6]](Wuhan_Greenland_Center#cite_note-6) surpassing the [Shanghai Tower](Shanghai_Tower "Shanghai Tower") by only 4.3 metres (14 ft) and the [Tokyo Skytree](Tokyo_Skytree "Tokyo Skytree") by 2.1 metres (7 ft), making it the second tallest man-made structure in the world. The tower was also supposed to have 126 floors, the second most of any building in the world, as well. When the Wuhan Greenland Center reached its 96th floor, construction was halted due to airspace restrictions which led to its subsequent redesign to a 476 metres (1,562 ft)[[7]](Wuhan_Greenland_Center#cite_note-7) building instead of a 636 metres (2,087 ft) building. The Wuhan Greenland Center is currently the [14th tallest building in the world](List_of_future_tallest_buildings "List of future tallest buildings").

Designed by [Adrian Smith + Gordon Gill Architecture](Adrian_Smith_%2B_Gordon_Gill_Architecture "Adrian Smith + Gordon Gill Architecture"), the building rises 1,550 feet (472.4 m) with 98 above-ground stories and three basement stories, although the top story is numbered 136. Central Park Tower is the [second-tallest building in New York City](List_of_tallest_buildings_in_New_York_City "List of tallest buildings in New York City"), [the United States](List_of_tallest_buildings_in_the_United_States "List of tallest buildings in the United States"), and the Western Hemisphere; the [15th tallest building in the world](List_of_tallest_buildings "List of tallest buildings"); the [tallest primarily residential building in the world](List_of_tallest_residential_buildings "List of tallest residential buildings"); and the tallest building outside Asia by roof height.

Central Park Tower was developed by [Extell Development Company](Extell_Development_Company "Extell Development Company") and [Shanghai Municipal Investment Group](Shanghai_Municipal_Investment_Group "Shanghai Municipal Investment Group"). The basement and first five above-ground stories contain a large <Nordstrom> store, which opened in 2019. The eastern portion of the tower contains a [cantilever](Cantilever "Cantilever") above the [Art Students League of New York](Art_Students_League_of_New_York "Art Students League of New York")'s building at [215 West 57th Street](American_Fine_Arts_Society "American Fine Arts Society"), intended to maximize views of nearby [Central Park](Central_Park "Central Park"). The residential portion of the tower contains 179 condominiums, spanning on average 5,000 sq ft (460 m2), with interiors designed by [Rottet Studio](Rottet_Studio "Rottet Studio"). There are also amenities spaces on floors 14 through 16 as well as a private club on floor 100.

The site of Central Park Tower was assembled during the first decade of the 21st century; during the acquisition process, the tower was delayed after two buildings at 225 West 57th Street and 1780 Broadway were considered for [New York City landmark](New_York_City_Landmarks_Preservation_Commission "New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission") status. Despite uncertainty about the final design and complications relating to financing, excavations at the site started in May 2014 and above-ground construction started in early 2015. There were several incidents and controversies during the building's construction, including a controversy over the tower's cantilever and the death of a security guard. The building was [topped out](Topping_out "Topping out") during September 2019, and completed in 2020. In total, Central Park Tower cost $3 billion to construct.

## Site

Central Park Tower is in the [Midtown Manhattan](Midtown_Manhattan "Midtown Manhattan") neighborhood of [New York City](New_York_City "New York City"), just south of [Columbus Circle](Columbus_Circle "Columbus Circle"), on the east side of [Broadway](Broadway_(Manhattan) "Broadway (Manhattan)") between [57th Street](57th_Street_(Manhattan) "57th Street (Manhattan)") to the south and 58th Street to the north. It is one block south of [Central Park](Central_Park "Central Park"). The northwestern corner of the building abuts [1790 Broadway](1790_Broadway "1790 Broadway"), while the southwestern corner is adjacent to 1776 Broadway. Central Park Tower is also near [240 Central Park South](240_Central_Park_South "240 Central Park South") and [220 Central Park South](220_Central_Park_South "220 Central Park South") to the north; the [American Fine Arts Society](American_Fine_Arts_Society "American Fine Arts Society") (also known as the [Art Students League of New York](Art_Students_League_of_New_York "Art Students League of New York") building) and [the Osborne](The_Osborne "The Osborne") apartment building to the east; and [224 West 57th Street](224_West_57th_Street "224 West 57th Street") and [218 West 57th Street](218_West_57th_Street "218 West 57th Street") (the former [American Society of Civil Engineers](American_Society_of_Civil_Engineers "American Society of Civil Engineers") clubhouse) to the south.[[3]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-4)

Central Park Tower is one of several major developments around 57th Street and Central Park that are collectively dubbed [Billionaires' Row](Billionaires'_Row_(Manhattan) "Billionaires' Row (Manhattan)") by the media. Other buildings along Billionaires' Row include [432 Park Avenue](432_Park_Avenue "432 Park Avenue") four blocks east, [111 West 57th Street](111_West_57th_Street "111 West 57th Street") and <One57> one block east, and the adjacent 220 Central Park South.[[4]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-5)[[5]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-6)[[6]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-Vanity_Fair-7)

### Former buildings

In the 20th century, the area was part of Manhattan's "Automobile Row", a stretch of Broadway extending mainly between [Times Square](Times_Square "Times Square") at [42nd Street](42nd_Street_(Manhattan) "42nd Street (Manhattan)") and [Sherman Square](Sherman_Square "Sherman Square") at [72nd Street](72nd_Street_(Manhattan) "72nd Street (Manhattan)").[[7]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-8)[[8]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-9) Before the first decade of the 20th century, the area was occupied mostly by equestrian industries and was described by *[The New York Times](The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")* as "thoroughly lifeless".[[9]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-nyt19070106-10) By 1907, the *Times* characterized this section of Broadway as having "almost a solid line of motor vehicle signs all the way from Times Square to Sherman Square".[[9]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-nyt19070106-10) In the late 1900s and early 1910s, several large automobile showrooms, stores, and garages were built on Broadway, including the [United States Rubber Company](United_States_Rubber_Company "United States Rubber Company") building at 5 Columbus Circle and the Demarest and Peerless Company showrooms at 224 West 57th Street.[[10]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-nyt19090221-11)

On the western side of the building's base is the 12-story facade of the former 1780 Broadway, which formerly contained the [B. F. Goodrich Company](B._F._Goodrich_Company "B. F. Goodrich Company") showroom.[[11]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-monster-12)[[12]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-Horsley_2009-13)[[13]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-nyt20081116-14) There was also an 8-story building at 225 West 57th Street,[[13]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-nyt20081116-14)[[14]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-NYCL_p._5-15) which contained the <Stoddard-Dayton> showroom.[[12]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-Horsley_2009-13)[[15]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-16) Both structures were built in 1909[[10]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-nyt19090221-11) to designs by [Howard Van Doren Shaw](Howard_Van_Doren_Shaw "Howard Van Doren Shaw").[[16]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-Barron_2011-17)[[14]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-NYCL_p._5-15) 1780 Broadway was one of the most visible buildings on Automobile Row because of the site's elevated topography,[[14]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-NYCL_p._5-15) and was leased to various automotive firms during the early 20th century.[[17]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-18) Goodrich came to own both 1780 Broadway and 225 West 57th Street, but by the time the company sold the structures in 1928, they were collectively called the "Goodrich Building".[[18]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-19) A single-story annex was built for the Lincoln Art Theatre in 1962–1964, and the Goodrich Building became a supermarket in the 1990s before being acquired by Extell in 2006.[[19]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-NYCL_p._7-20) In addition, the [Hard Rock Cafe](Hard_Rock_Cafe "Hard Rock Cafe") and [Broadway Dance Center](Broadway_Dance_Center "Broadway Dance Center") occupied the structure at 221 West 57th Street before that building was purchased by Central Park Tower's developer, the [Extell Development Company](Extell_Development_Company "Extell Development Company"), in 2006.[[11]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-monster-12)

## Architecture

Central Park Tower was developed jointly by Extell and [Shanghai Municipal Investment Group](Shanghai_Municipal_Investment_Group "Shanghai Municipal Investment Group").[[20]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-Bloomberg-21)[[21]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-22) It was designed by [Adrian Smith + Gordon Gill Architecture](Adrian_Smith_%2B_Gordon_Gill_Architecture "Adrian Smith + Gordon Gill Architecture").[[22]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-Dezeen_2019-23)[[23]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-24)[[24]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-25) [WSP Global](WSP_Global "WSP Global") was the structural engineer for the project, while <Lendlease> was the main contractor.[[1]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-The_Skyscraper_Center_2016-1)

The building has 98 physical above-ground floors[[1]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-The_Skyscraper_Center_2016-1)[[25]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-Warren_2020-26) and three basement levels.[[1]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-The_Skyscraper_Center_2016-1)[[26]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-Extell_pp._311-317-27) The top story is numbered 136,[[2]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-Extell_p._317-2) and several floor numbers are skipped.[[27]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-Extell_p._308-28)[[lower-alpha 2]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-marketing_floors-29) The tallest habitable story is 1,417 feet (432 m) high,[[1]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-The_Skyscraper_Center_2016-1) while the roof and architectural tip are 1,550 feet (470 m) above ground level.[[1]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-The_Skyscraper_Center_2016-1)[[28]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-Emporis-30)[[29]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-31) The use of [development rights](Air_rights "Air rights") transferred from other structures nearby, as well as about 300 feet (91 m) of mechanical spaces, enabled Central Park Tower to reach a taller height than would have ordinarily been allowed.[[30]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-nyt20190614-32) Central Park Tower is the [tallest primarily residential building in the world](List_of_tallest_residential_buildings "List of tallest residential buildings"); the much taller [Burj Khalifa](Burj_Khalifa "Burj Khalifa") has 900 residential units but is mixed-use.[[31]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-33) Central Park Tower is also the [second-tallest skyscraper in the United States and the Western Hemisphere](List_of_tallest_buildings_in_the_United_States "List of tallest buildings in the United States"), the [15th-tallest building in the world](List_of_tallest_buildings "List of tallest buildings"), and the tallest building outside Asia by roof height.[[32]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-34) The building's top floor and roof height are higher than that of [One World Trade Center](One_World_Trade_Center "One World Trade Center") in [Lower Manhattan](Lower_Manhattan "Lower Manhattan"); additionally, the building sits on higher ground, further increasing its topological prominence. Due to its high [slenderness ratio](Slenderness_ratio "Slenderness ratio"), the building has been characterized as part of a new breed of New York City "[pencil towers](Pencil_tower "Pencil tower")".[[33]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-35)

### Form and facade

The facade of Central Park Tower was designed by James Carpenter Design Associates and Permasteelisa Group.[[1]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-The_Skyscraper_Center_2016-1) According to Gill and Smith, the glass cladding was intended to help the tower fit into the skyline.[[34]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-The_Architects_Newspaper_2019-36) The entrance for Nordstrom is on 57th Street, as is the main residential entrance. A secondary residents' entrance is on 58th Street.[[35]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-37)[[36]](Central_Park_Tower#cite_note-Extell_pp._324-325-38)

To maximize views of Central Park, Extell built a [cantilever](Cantilever "Cantilever") extending 28 feet (8.5 m) from the eastern side of the tower.
